bull_bear.body: - FY27 capex ₹1,500cr (frontloaded). Conservative guidance, broad-based capacity ahead of demand.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Metal-price / war / freight volatility → near-term demand & margin (the headline risk this call).
- Middle-East exposure: oil sourcing (Saudi Aramco Yanbu refinery — still running) + sales to Saudi/Kuwait/Iraq subdued until war ends.
- New competition: **UltraTech (Aditya Birla) + Adani** entering wires/cables (mostly building wires/LDC — mgmt says limited threat to specialty); a new conductor entrant with "carbon-core" tech near PGCIL approval (past-performance tender requirement is a barrier).
- US Section 232: 50% on conductors (Al), 25% on cables — now stable (certainty = positive); US imports ~90% Al (so US producers also pay duty) vs <5% Cu → Al exports less disadvantaged.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Conservative guidance (under-promises margins), candid on near-term headwinds, deeply entrenched (sole HVDC-oil supplier; CTC pressure from transformer OEMs). Frontloading capex on conviction in the multi-year cycle.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Two-speed read:** structural demand intact, but Apar is the one name flagging a *real near-term air-pocket* (metal prices + war) — a useful caution vs the suppliers riding the shortage. Watch whether others echo this next quarter.
- **Apar confirms KSH's thesis from the buyer side:** CTC was in "major domestic deficit" — Apar (a CTC maker itself) prioritized domestic transformer OEMs and only now exports.
- **HVDC transformer-oil monopoly** (Hitachi/GE/Siemens) is a quiet, high-moat annuity as HVDC awards flow FY27–28.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet remains conservatively geared with a debt/equity ratio of 0.16x in FY26 versus 0.10x in FY24 and FY25, despite the step-up in capex.
- Growth is being funded largely from internal accruals, with capex rising to Rs 736.66 crore in FY26 while working capital was Rs 3,252.86 crore.
- Capex is spread across segments rather than concentrated — conductors, oils and cables all received investment across FY24-FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Clean energy: **50GW+ added FY26** (highest ever); non-fossil 250–270GW; solar 140GW+ (record +54GW FY26); wind +6GW.
- **Transformation capacity +113,000 MVA FY26** (+30% YoY, ~11% below the 126k target); **48% at 765kV**.
- Data centres: 1.5–1.7GW → **5GW by 2030** (7–8GW optimistic), >$30bn investment.
- NEP to 2032: transmission 5L→6.5L ckm; transformation 1,429→2,354 GVA; interregional 120→143GW (2027)→168GW (2032).
business.title: Macro backdrop (useful sector data)

business.body:
- **Short-term slowdown in ordering** — aluminium price + premiums (MJP) up, freight/war premiums at all-time highs, Middle-East containers shipping without full insurance → **projects deferred/delayed**; customers postpone deliveries (even OPGW/fibre, costs up 3–4x).
- **Manpower/port issues** from elections (Bihar/West Bengal/NE) slowing project execution.
- Domestic capacity additions → some pricing pressure; Chinese competition; LME–SHFE aluminium gap $330–360/t.
- *But:* "structurally, energy-infrastructure fundamentals remain intact" — expects a 2H-weighted year (like FY26).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Claims #1 position in India by conductor sales in FY26 and is one of the leading global aluminium and alloy conductor manufacturers as of March 2026, alongside being one of India's leading exporters of conductors and cables.
- India's largest private sector manufacturer of specialty oils by installed capacity as of March 2026, and one of the largest cable manufacturers for the domestic renewables segment.
- 68-year legacy operating 11 facilities globally with corporate presence in six countries (India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, USA, Singapore, Brazil) and ~2,200 employees.
- Serves a diversified global customer base across T&D, mobility, telecom, infrastructure, renewables, data centres and defence, positioned around three themes: Carrying Electricity, Client-First Innovation and Engineered Performance.
- Growth is framed around established drivers (renewables, transmission, infrastructure, public transport, telecom, China+1) plus two newer drivers witnessed in the last two years — data centre buildout and energy storage systems.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Customer mix] FY26 customer mix is led by exports (29-30%), industries/corporates (18-19%), EPC transmission companies (14-15%) and OEMs (11-12%), with the deck noting limited exposure to state-owned electricity distribution boards after the mix shift.
- [Receivables quality] 50.40% of FY26 receivables are secured under various means and a further 25.40% are from government transmission and sector-specific companies, leaving 24.20% as others.
- [Export franchise] Export mix was 29.77% in FY26, having moderated from 32.82% in FY24, with exports of Rs 6,817.96 crore in FY26.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Conductor unit margin up on **premium mix (45.8%) + rising copper mix**; metal-price rise also lifts interest cost (so EBITDA, pre-interest, benefits from tailwinds).
- Oil EBITDA/KL slightly down (forex provision ₹15cr in March; Middle-East export hit).
- Cables: **specialty-polymer shortage** (sourced from Abu Dhabi/Middle East) + Al/Cu/polymer price spikes → near-term volume & margin pressure; limits aggressive specialty-cable booking.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** record yr ₹22,902cr (+23%); conductors crossed ₹10,000cr at ₹43k/MT; cables #2 (DC-led, US $15m to 3 projects); HVDC-oil orders awaited FY27-28; CTC exports starting; **flagged near-term slowdown** (metals/war/manpower); FY27 capex ₹1,500cr.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: did the near-term slowdown bite (volume/margin)?, US ramp, HVDC-oil order awards, CTC export approvals (EU/US), conductor margin vs ₹35–36k+tailwinds, cable toward ₹10,000cr._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Conductor EBITDA/MT: ₹35,000–36,000 + tailwinds** (vs FY26 actual ₹43,012 — i.e. conservative; premium/copper mix supportive). Raised over time (was ₹8–10k → ₹30k → ₹35–36k).
- **Volume:** Conductor **+10%/yr**; **Cables +25%/yr** (25% CAGR toward ₹10,000cr cable revenue).
- **US:** "significant growth FY27 over FY26" in both cables and conductors as tariffs settle.
- **FY27 capex ₹1,500cr** (vs ₹740cr FY26): Cable ₹850cr · Conductor ₹400cr · Oil ₹200cr — pulled forward (longer capex cycle).

outlook.body:
- Conductor OB ₹7,671cr (premium >50% of OB). Cable pending ~₹1,800cr. (Oil is contract/spot.)
- **HVDC** projects **just awarded** → conductor + oil orders flow **FY27–FY28** (APAR = principal/only HVDC transformer-oil supplier to Hitachi Energy, GE, Siemens).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Data centres (US-led):** supplied 3 US DC projects (~$15m cables); a medium US DC = **$25–30m of cables**; India 50MW DC ≈ ₹2cr (100MW ≈ ₹5–6cr). US spec >> India; AI DC BoM evolving with NVIDIA chips. Dedicated US-spec DC-cable capex. *No capacity-blocking by hyperscalers* (routed via EPCs).
- **CTC exports:** after 5 expansion phases, now exporting CTC (Middle East approved; pursuing Europe/US) — previously domestic-only due to **"major deficit in the domestic market."**
- **Renewables/railways/defence cables;** reconducting/upgradation of aging lines; UHV/HVDC.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: The diversified T&D bellwether (₹22,902cr, ~29% 5-yr CAGR). Conductors crossed ₹10,000cr at record unit margins; cables now #2 segment (data-centre led); **sole HVDC transformer-oil supplier** to Hitachi/GE/Siemens. Confirms the structural super-cycle *and* that **CTC was in domestic deficit** (now exporting). But uniquely flags a **near-term demand slowdown** — metal-price spikes, war/freight premiums, and election-driven manpower issues are making customers postpone deliveries. Margins guided conservatively to ₹35–36k/MT **+ tailwinds**.

open.item: Copper business (conductors, CTC, busbars) expected to exceed INR3,000 crores next year (FY26).
INR1,300cr capex to be funded ~50:50 by internal accruals/equity (INR650cr) and long-term debt (INR650cr).
After 5 phases of CTC capacity expansion, APAR has begun exporting CTC (Middle East approvals secured) and is pursuing Europe and US approvals to broaden CTC exports in FY27/FY28.

Bushing shortage delaying transformer/substation deliveries and hence transmission-line/CTC/transformer-oil demand; government import concession kicking in within ~1 week and domestic bushing capacity expected in ~6 months.

Near-term demand slowdown flagged: sharp metal (Al/Cu) and freight/war-premium cost increases and specialty-polymer shortages will hit near-term cable/conductor/oil volumes and margins as customers defer deliveries.
US sales expected to grow significantly in FY27 over FY26 (and further in FY28) for both cables and conductors, aided by settled Section 232 tariffs (25% on cables, 50% aluminium conductors).
Conductor volume growth guidance maintained at ~10% year-on-year (FY26 delivered 8.6%).
FY27 capex increased to ~INR1,500 crores (conductor ~INR400cr, oil ~INR200cr, cable ~INR850cr), on top of FY26 capex of INR740 crores, front-loaded for future demand.
APAR is the sole HVDC transformer-oil supplier to Hitachi Energy, GE and Siemens; large HVDC projects just awarded, with oil/conductor order awards to flow through FY27 and FY28.
Cable division targeting ~25% CAGR toward INR10,000 crores (FY26 at INR6,220cr, +25.8%); capex being pulled forward, tracking on/slightly ahead.
Long-term (3-5 year) sustainable conductor EBITDA per metric ton guided at INR28,500 plus tailwinds.

Middle East war severely disrupted oil supply chain (refinery raw-material stranding, April contract supplies down 50%, freight spikes); oil/Specialty exports and some conductor (Iraq) deliveries subdued until the war resolves; supply largely restored in May at higher prices.
Conductor medium-to-long-term EBITDA/ton guidance upgraded to INR35,000-36,000 plus tailwinds (from INR30,000), on premium/reconductoring/copper mix.
US manufacturing set-up still under study given a fluid tariff/policy situation; decision to be taken as clarity emerges.

India-EU FTA expected to be favourable for cable/conductor exports (EU ~5% of revenue; prior tariffs 4-7.5% plus OFC antidumping); pursuing more EU utility approvals, impact to be quantified in a couple of months.
Chinese subsidy (~8-12% on metal) making non-US export markets (Africa, LatAm, Europe, Australia) unattractive; APAR will divert capacity to India rather than compete at a loss; seen as cyclical.
Appointed advisors to explore setting up manufacturing in the US (over and above the announced India/UAE capex) to serve US-made-product utilities and short-delivery demand.
Amended articles of association to permit entry into the energy storage business as a future line; at a very early exploratory stage.
Chinese competition (often below-cost pricing) has intensified and is expected to continue in all markets except India and the US; management will not cut prices merely for volume.
Conductor EBITDA per ton guidance retained at INR28,500 (currently realizing ~INR37,000-38,000 on premium mix).
